title: Hurricanes hit the Homeland: ONG members aid fellow Americans
description: Three major hurricanes hit the mainland U.S. or two of its territories during the 2017 Atlantic hurricane season. Since the first storm made landfall in August, more than 400 members of the Ohio National Guard were engaged with rescue and relief efforts in Texas, Florida, the U.S. Virgin Islands, and Puerto Rico.
keywords: response, Maria, Harvey, relief, hurricanes, U.S. Virgin Islands, ong, Irma, soldier, National Guard, AIr Force, Ohio, army, Texas, Florida, airman, Puerto Rico

transcript.text: ^- [Stephanie] Hurricane Harvey in Texas.
^Hurricane Irma, Florida and the U.S. Virgin Islands.
^Hurricane Maria in Puerto Rico.
The 2017 Atlantic Hurricane Season had a succession
of major hurricanes.
Since the first storm made landfall in August,
more than 400 men and women of the Ohio National Guard
had been engaged in rescue and relief efforts.
Two Ohio Army National Guard CH-47 Chinook helicopters
were one of the first to respond
after Hurricane Harvey hit Texas.
The crews worked to transport water, food,
fuel for other helicopters, and personnel,
even bales of hay for cattle stuck in fields
that became islands after the hurricane's flood waters.
Food and shelter for all of the first responders
was also a priority during the recovery efforts.
The 200th Red Horse Squadron set up
disaster relief bed down systems
in Saint Thomas, U.S. Virgin Islands, and Puerto Rico.
Each system provided basic life needs
such as shelter, showers, and laundry.
Back to back hurricanes made it challenging
for the team while in the Virgin Islands.
- We were here right after Irma.
^We built up base camp, and then Maria came through
^so we had to evacuate, tear the entire tent city down,
^tear everything down, evacuate to Florida.
^Then once Maria came through, come back down
and rebuild everything right back up again.
- [Stephanie] Airmen from the 179th Airlift Wing, Mansfield,
and 178th Wing, Springfield, served about 9400 meals
during the month they operated a disaster relief
mobile kitchen trailer in Puerto Rico.
Also in Puerto Rico, with sports arenas serving
as their base of operations,
combat medics with the 285th Medical Company,
assisted more than 2000 patients
at different locations while deployed.
There are many stories of residents expressing their thanks
for the selfless service provided
by Ohio National Guard members.
^- People would come up to us and hug us
^and thank us for all our help.
^Didn't matter what our job was,
^we were there to do anything we could to help,
and they were appreciative of it.
- [Stephanie] Additional logistical support came
in the form of transportation, communications,
chaplaincy, public affairs, imagery analysis,
from Ohio Airmen and Soldiers in eight units
and all four Air National Guard Wings.
(calm music)
